value.name: SNAP/EBT
value.redemption_instructions: Most outdoor farmers can't swipe EBT, so get gold SNAP tokens at the Market Center (or the Education Center on weekends). Butchers take EBT directly.

value.name: Produce Perks
value.note: Each $1 in SNAP tokens is matched with $1 in green Produce Perks tokens, up to $25 a day. Produce Perks tokens are for produce only.

value.stop_name: Station 10 (Elm St, northbound) and Station 12 (Race St, southbound)

location_note.value: The North Lot (off Findlay St) and South Lot (off Race St) cost $3 an hour, paid by plate or with Cincy EZPark zone 4523. Merchants hand out discount codes.

value.note: Education Center, the red booth next to the Farm Shed in the North Lot: Fri 11am-4pm, Sat 8am-3pm, Sun 9am-3pm. The Market Center desk in the market house helps when it is closed.
Live music on weekends at Race St. Station, open Sat-Sun 11am-4pm, with plenty of seating.

value.name: Education Center
value.description: Staffed weekend resource center for SNAP and Produce Perks redemption, seasonal recipe cards, and SFMNP and TANF applications.

value.name: Community Resource Tent
value.description: Each weekend a nonprofit or community group tables at the Outdoor Market with information and resources.

value.answer: The market house is open Tuesday through Sunday year-round. The Farm Shed farmers market runs only on weekends: Saturday 8am-2pm and Sunday 10am-2pm. Mondays are closed.
The North and South lots cost $3 an hour. Pay by plate at the stations or use Cincy EZPark zone 4523, and ask a merchant for a discount code after you buy something.
Most outdoor farmers can't swipe EBT. Get gold SNAP tokens at the Market Center or Education Center, plus matching green Produce Perks tokens for produce, up to $25 a day.
Holiday hours for 2026: closed Thanksgiving (Nov 26), Christmas Day and New Year's Day, with 9am-3pm hours on Nov 11, Nov 23, Dec 21, Dec 24 and Dec 31.

operator_name.value: City of St. Louis Department of Parks, Recreation and Forestry

location_note.value: Metered street parking around the market, plus a free public lot across from 7th Street and Carroll Street.

value.note: Animals are prohibited anywhere on market grounds.
Smoking is prohibited anywhere on market grounds.

value.answer: Saturday is the full market day with every vendor in. Only about 10% of vendors open Wednesday and Thursday, and about 35% on Friday.
The market is closed Sunday through Tuesday, except one produce stand on Sundays. Call the market at (314) 622-4180 before coming on a Sunday.
There is metered street parking around the market and a free public lot across from 7th Street and Carroll Street.
The market is open year round, but individual vendor hours may vary.

availability_note.value: Foodwise's October picks for its farmers markets include apples, pears, persimmons, pomegranates, quince, winter squash, chestnuts, and new-crop walnuts and almonds.

value.name: Fall Fruit Celebration
value.description: Seasonal Spotlight celebration of fall fruit with free samples, recipes, and a variety tasting at the orange tent in front of the Ferry Building, plus an 11am cooking demo.

value.name: Fall Holiday Farmers Market
value.description: The regular Tuesday farms plus special guest vendors, for stocking up before Thanksgiving.

value.name: Pop-Ups on the Plaza: Black Holiday Market
value.description: Holiday market of Bay Area Black-owned food makers and designers. Free entry.
value.venue: South arcade of the Ferry Building

value.answer: Saturday is the big market, with more than 100 vendors around the Ferry Building. Tuesday has about 20 vendors focused on produce and hot lunch, and Thursday has 10 to 15 vendors, mostly street food lunch plus produce.
The Thursday market is closed on November 26, December 24, and December 31, 2026. A special Fall Holiday Farmers Market runs Tuesday, November 24, 10am-2pm.
Lost items go to the Ferry Building Lost & Found at the Security Desk in the office lobby, first floor on the Embarcadero side. Phone 415-983-8007.

value.name: SNAP EBT
value.redemption_instructions: Go to the market information tent, swipe your EBT card and enter your PIN to buy $1 or $5 wooden tokens that spend like cash. Unused tokens do not expire.

value.name: Farmers Market Nutrition Program
value.redemption_instructions: Pay the farmer directly with $5 FMNP checks for fresh fruits and vegetables. No change is given.

value.name: Healthfirst OTC (select plans)
value.redemption_instructions: Bring your OTC card to the market information tent to exchange OTC dollars for $2 Greenmarket Bucks.

value.name: Health Bucks
value.note: Up to $10 per day. Health Bucks expire December 31 each year.

value.name: Greenmarket Bucks
value.note: $2 coupons accepted at all Greenmarkets, given out by partner organizations; they expire December 31 each year.

availability_note.value: GrowNYC's seasonal guide lists fall picks like apples, Concord grapes, Seckel pears, winter squash, Brussels sprouts and root vegetables. It is a regional guide, not a list of what is at this market today.

value.name: 6th Annual Cider Village
value.description: Tastings from eight New York cideries, an apple cider donut eating contest, apple trivia and rare apple varieties. Rescheduled from the October 16 rain date.

value.name: Cultured book signing with Richard Martin
value.description: Book signing for Cultured: A Global Guide to Fermenting and Preserving Fruit, Vegetables, Dairy, and Grains.

value.name: Día de los Muertos with Luna Family Farm
value.description: Bring a photo of a loved one to place on Luna Family Farm's ofrenda.

value.name: Mediterranean All the Way book signing with Ayesha Nurdjaja
Radicchio book signing with Lane Selman
Compost drop-off
value.description: Compost is collected Monday, Wednesday, Friday and Saturday, 8:00 am - 5:00 pm, an hour before the market closes.

value.name: Cooking demos and family activities
value.description: Cooking demonstrations, educational programs and activities for families at the market.

value.answer: The market runs year round on Mondays, Wednesdays, Fridays and Saturdays, 8am-6pm, along 17th Street and Union Square West.
Bring your EBT card and PIN to the green information tent to buy wooden tokens. Every $2 in SNAP earns a $2 Health Buck for fruits and vegetables, up to $10 a day.
Up to 140 regional farmers, fishers and bakers sell here in peak season. The lineup changes by day, so check GrowNYC's producer list for the day you plan to visit.

value.name: SNAP / Bridge Card
value.redemption_instructions: Many vendors accept Bridge Cards. Ask at the Welcome Center or the Shed 5 Information Booth for how to use your card at the market.

value.name: WIC Produce Connect
value.redemption_instructions: Michigan farmers can accept WIC Produce Connect cards May through October at the Saturday and Tuesday markets. Ask at the Welcome Center or Shed 5 Information Booth which vendors accept it.

value.name: Senior Project FRESH
value.redemption_instructions: Michigan farmers can accept Senior Project FRESH cards May through October at the Saturday and Tuesday markets. Ask at the Welcome Center or Shed 5 Information Booth which vendors accept it.

value.name: Double Up Food Bucks
value.note: Matches SNAP purchases dollar-for-dollar, up to $50 per day.

location_note.value: Parking is free throughout most of the district. Street parking tickets are $45, so check signs.

accessibility_note.value: The market says it is accessible for wheelchairs and strollers.

value.note: Welcome Center on the south side of Shed 3, and an Information Booth inside Shed 5.
Dogs and other animals are not allowed in sheds, covered structures, or near vendor stalls, except registered service animals. Dogs are welcome elsewhere in the district.
No smoking or vaping in sheds, covered structures, or near vendor stalls.

availability_note.value: Eastern Market publishes a seasonal produce calendar on its Explore the Market page showing when Michigan fruits and vegetables are in season.

value.answer: Besides the year-round Saturday Market, there is a Flower Tuesday Market every Tuesday in May (9am-3pm) and summer markets June-September: Sunday Street Market 10am-4pm and Tuesday Health and Wellness Market 9am-3pm.
The Wholesale Market is open to the public for bulk purchases only, midnight-6am, Monday-Friday, April-November.
Flower Day is the Sunday after Mother's Day each year. Saturday Markets typically have a wide selection of flowers from mid-April through June.
Christmas tree vendors set up in the parking lot outside Sheds 5 and 6, seven days a week, starting around Thanksgiving.
